description.narrative: The Swedish support to the Mozambique statistics system through the UNFPA Trust Fund is aiming to give the government, public and private sectors, civil society and others access to reliable, updated and consistent demographic, social and economic statistics. Outcome: By making accurate data accessible for all it is expected that there will be improved planning and use of public resources, fact-based political decisions and in general an increased transparency and access to information. Impact: With published data in 2018 and 2019 the 2017 Population Census is expected to be a catalyst to further a wider policy agenda related to creating a stronger data based policy culture. Outcomes/activities: 1) strengthening human and institutional resources ensuring quality collection and data analysis; 2) increasing the capabilities of national agencies to plan, prepare and generate quality population census data; and 3) strengthening communication, confidence building and data culture promoting an inclusive census. Specific focus on capturing data on living conditions for women and girls, and for persons living with disabilities will help gathering more information on vulnerability and exclusion.

Insatsen är ett stöd till Moçambiques statistikmyndighet INE och dess produktion av befolknings-, social, jämställdhets- och ekonomisk statistik. Under 2017 genomfördes en folkräkning där det nu finns en stor mängd data att behandla under 2018 och 2019. Särskilt fokus kommer därför att vara på folkräkningsrelaterade aktiviteter.
Bidraget går via UNFPAs statistikfond (Trust Fund) under åren 2018-2019 och har som mål att såväl offentlig som privat sektorn, civilsamhället och media ska ha tillgång till och kunna använda sig av tillförlitlig och konsistent, uppdaterad statistik och -analys. Med detta förväntas Moçambique få bättre möjligheter för statlig(t) planering och genomförande, stärkt ansvarsutkrävande, politiska beslut fattade på sakliga grunder samt en förbättrad uppföljning av utvecklingen i landet.
Detta ska åstadkommas genom 1) institutionell kapacitetsuppbyggnad kring statistisk kvalitet i datainsamling och analys; 2) stärkande av regionala statistikkontor (INE:s provinsavdelningar) och deras kapacitet att planera, samla in och generera relevant och tillförlitlig befolkningsstatistik; och 3) stärkt förmåga på INE att kommunicera och nå ut till allmänheten kring statistik, samt att också bättre fånga upp och nå utsatta eller underrepresenterade grupper i samhället i sin datainsamling (framför allt kvinnor och flickor, samt människor som lever med funktionshinder).

The contribution is a support to the statistical agency INE and its production of population, social, gender and economic statistics. During 2017 a population and housing census was conducted with a massive data set to process during 2018 and 2019. Specific focus is therefore on the activities related to the census. The support is channelled through UNFPAs Statistics Trust Fund. It aims to give the public and private sectors as well as civil society and media access to and use reliable and consistent population data and analysis.
Three outputs are designed to work in support of the outcome: Output 1: Human and institutional capacity strengthened ensuring quality collection and data analysis. Output 2: Increased capabilities of national and provincial agencies to plan, prepare and generate quality population census data on households, women and men. Output 3: Strengthened communication, confidence building and data culture promoting an inclusive census (specifically for girls and women, and for persons living with disabilities).

The project made substantial progress in all main areas of focus. In some cases, it exceeded the expectes results. Below are examples of results achieved during the reported period, March 2018 to June 2023:
- Complete enumeration of the 2017 Mozambiques 4th Population and Housing Census (MPHC) - Release of the final official results of the 2017 4th MPHC - Complete tabulations, disaggregation and projection of the 2017 Census results, to subnational level-- - Innovative dissemination of Census results in form of Demographic Atlas (National and Provincial) and Georeferenced Maps (clearly presenting the spatial distribution of the population at subnational level in relation and socio and economic infrastructure) - Revitalisation and strengthening of INE´s Gender Statistics Function leading to mainstreaming of Gender Statistics in INEs routine functions - 17 Thematic Studies based on the results of the 2017 MPHC written and published - 5,000 National Statistical System (SEN) staff (of which 40% women) had their technical and managerial capacities strengthened over a broad range of statistical technical issues and other operations - Enhanced utilisation of official statistics as evidenced from the Policy and Planning papers written by the Government Agencies relying on INEs official statistics - Evidence based humanitarian responses relying on INEs official data in general and 2017 MPHC results in particular - Improved financial management and assurance capacity of INE as evidenced from 3 unqualified audits during the 5 years of the Project´s implementation and Contributed to the realisation of the 202223 Demographic and Health Survey (DHS).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
